The Proof Page

Every call LongShotWolf made on the record — the spread calls and the three-minute reads — timestamped when it fired, then graded against what the tape actually did. The misses are on this page, right next to the hits. Nobody else in this market publishes theirs.

Signal rooms charge $50–$225 a month on claimed win rates. This page is the audit before anyone pays a cent: 1,517 entries — 1,180 graded calls: the 562 spread calls of Weeks 1–3, graded mechanically under rules locked on Oct 24, 2026 and never loosened since, and 618 three-minute calls, every one on Litecoin, backfilled on his Nov 15, 2026 ruling and graded under his mechanical 3M doctrine — plus 337 Four Points level touches, every one a DIRECT HIT, each printed in full below. Read the whole sheet, check any row against the public posts, then decide what a seat is worth.

The candle finals

Every 6H candle close, the final spread declares a band. Did the candle's full travel back it up?
167 / 167

Band-declaring candle finals graded HIT. Zero misses.

Across all three weeks, every time a 6H candle closed outside the quiet zone — 167 finals, from BTC's −$2,627.88 BIG BIG MOVE close on Oct 29 through Candle 88's +$338.9 BTC A CYCLE final on Nov 15 — the declared band matched the candle's actual travel from its anchor.

The other 140 finals closed in the quiet or low band. They declare no band, so they are marked UNGRADED — listed in full in the ledger, counted neither for nor against the record.

How every row is graded

Locked Oct 24, 2026. Never loosened retroactively — Week 1 keeps its original grades, untouched.

The window

Each call is graded from the minute it fired to the close of the 6H candle it was made in, against Bitunix futures tape. The call was posted publicly first — in Discord #spread-reading, the army spread rooms, or Kick chat — so the timestamp exists outside this page.

The bands

BTC: cycle $300 · a move $500 · better $800 · big big $1,000. LTC: cycle $0.60 · big $1.00. ETH: provisional $15 / $30. A band call is a HIT when price runs the floor in the called direction; a MISS when it first travels more than half the floor the other way; in between is PARTIAL — direction right, size short.

The 20% range rule

From Week 2, by his teaching: a call is a range, not a point — "you can never really call a direct hit on any coin, by the way they move." A run reaching 80% of the floor grades HIT; 50–80% grades SHORT. Every row shows the actual run next to the call, with a closeness stamp — within 10% / 15% / 20% of the call, or past the number.

What is not on this sheet: Field Radar readings (scheduled system reports, not his calls), battlefield board flips, and dictated ad reads. The sheet holds his calls only — that's what makes it proof of the reader, not of the machinery around him.

Week 3 — candles 23–64, locked

Oct 29, 5 PM – Nov 9, 5 AM Phoenix · graded in the Nov 9, 2026 weekly refresh

Week 3 picks up where Week 2 locked — Candle 23 through Candle 64 — and it is the biggest sheet yet: 166 rows. The finals streak held: 64 band-declaring finals, all graded HIT, against 62 quiet finals marked UNGRADED. The live reads ran harder: 36 band calls went 10 HIT · 26 MISS, and all four of the week's temp calls graded MISS — the running tally now stands at 5 TEMP TOPS · 7 TEMP BOTTOMS. Candle 65 (Nov 9) was still open when this grading locked, so it is not on the sheet. Every Week 3 row sits in the ledger above — filter to Week 3 to read them.

Method & disclosures — from the Week 3 ledger

HA CHAIN VERIFIED END TO END: anchors for candles 23-64 were chained from the locked candle-23 anchors (BTC 79996.1533 / LTC 57.1442 / ETH 2313.4181, candles20-22 close-out) over the Bitunix 6H tape. The chain lands on the recorded candle-65 anchors (~/hooks/state/anchors.json: BTC 74708.58098090625 / LTC 50.692904140625 / ETH 2139.674015) with a difference of 0.000000 on all three coins, and reproduces candle 64's settled finals exactly (BTC -747.89 / LTC -8.33c / ETH -53.12). Every hook print's implied anchor (live - spread) also matches the chain anchor for its candle, except the one stale-anchor print disclosed on its row (candle 51).

EXCURSION GRANULARITY: band-call and temp-call excursions were graded on Bitunix 1m klines (fetched for every candle carrying a call; all 360 bars present per candle). Two grades changed versus a 3m first pass — candle 53's BTC -$704.7 print grades HIT at 1m (the adverse spike sat in the print's own 3m bar, before the print tick).

HOOK COVERAGE GAPS (never guessed, no prints invented): the hook print logs on record begin BTC Nov 4 08:29Z (candle 44), LTC Nov 6 22:37Z (candle 54), ETH Nov 7 03:08Z (candle 55). Candles before those points carry finals only, exactly as candles 15-22 did in Week 2 when the hooks were unarmed. Two same-crossing double-fires (BTC candle 46, 18:04:37Z/18:04:55Z; BTC candle 50, 18:08:11Z/18:08:27Z — state races seconds apart) were counted once each.

DISCORD: this run graded from the hook print logs, the Kick chat feed captures and the Bitunix tape. The #spread-reading channel itself was not independently re-read in this run (no Discord read tool was available to the grading worker); the hook prints graded here are the prints the hooks fired and posted in real time.

CHAT SWEEP: every candle's calls.jsonl window was swept (captured/is_call counts are in each candle note). Flagged entries that are proximity reads ('close to the temp top', 'getting close to the temp bottom'), emote-only temp markers, an unpinnable '$30 spread' read, and the Nov 5 '1000$ spread' remark (tape spread already -$3,306.74 when typed — the move had already happened and its crossings are this candle's hook prints) were examined and NOT counted as calls; each is disclosed in its candle note.

CANDLE 65 (Nov 9, 5am-11am Phoenix) was still open at run time (10:38 AM MST) and is NOT graded here; its hook prints on record so far stay out of the ledger until its close is graded in order.

Four Points

Every recorded touch of a marked Four Points level — each one a DIRECT HIT, each printed in full, times in New York.

Four Points is the level system riding beside the spread record: for each of the big 3, on the 6H, day, week and month candles, the system marks four levels — Point 1, the end of candle away from the wick; Point 2; Point 3, where candle and wick meet; and Point 4. When live price reaches a marked level, the watcher fires at that moment and posts the hit to the channel. On the Warlord's order (Nov 13, 2026), every one of those hits is on this page — the whole record, back to the first hit the watcher ever logged — each graded DIRECT HIT and counted in the combined record above, and each carrying its full description of what it did. New hits flow onto this page on every refresh from here on.

His 3-minute slowing and pushing reads — every one graded against the 3M tape, times in New York. All 618 on Litecoin.

These are his shortest reads: on the 3-minute Heikin-Ashi frame he calls an army slowing or pushing, and the two candles after the call settle it. On the Warlord's ruling (Nov 15, 2026), the three-minute calls are graded entries on this page — backfilled as far as the surviving record reaches, to Oct 25, 2026, the first 3M read in the surviving Kick chat capture — and they count in the record like every other call on the sheet: all 618 sit inside the calls-only book and the combined book at the top of this page. Every one is on Litecoin, his coin, and every one is printed in full below, hits and misses alike: 158 HIT · 460 MISS.

THREE-MINUTE CALLS — 618 GRADED CALLS · 158 HIT · 460 MISS
ALL 618 ON LITECOIN — HIS COIN, AND THE COIN THE 3M READ WAS TAUGHT ON
What happened — every count in this box is a call he actually made: 616 typed in his own Kick chat, and 2 spoken on the Nov 15, 2026 voice call and marked spoken on their rows — each one graded mechanically over the two 3-minute candles after it, under the doctrine set out in the method below. The misses are printed at the same size as the hits — all 460 of them.

The record runs from the first call on Oct 25, 2026 to the latest on Nov 15, 2026 — the two spoken calls, M3-617 and M3-618, close the sheet, their spoken-call disclosure carried in their own descriptions. Method & disclosures — from the three-minute ledger

BACKGRADE ORDER (Nov 15, 2026): the Warlord ruled 'Go back as far as you can go back and put them on the proof page.' This ledger grades his 3-minute slowing/pushing calls as real graded entries. It supersedes the house's older convention, under which his typed 'slowing on the 3 min' reads were disclosed in candle notes as proximity reads and NOT graded; that convention was the house's, and the record now follows his ruling.

REACH: the earliest call graded here is at 2026-10-25T05:21:11Z — the first 3M read in the surviving Kick chat capture. The capture itself begins 2026-10-25 05:20Z; before that the trail genuinely ends — no earlier call is entered, because none survives to grade.

SOURCES in his order of trust: (a) his own free-typed Kick chat lines (pasted house posts never count) — 616 entries; (b) 3M reads quoted verbatim in the old candle notes, each cited to its note in its source field — the notes were swept and every 3M read they quote was already in the chat capture, so this source adds no separate entries — nothing was double-counted. (c) the two LTC calls he SPOKE on the Nov 15, 2026 voice call, marked spoken and confirmed against the shared engine at the time — 2 entries. A house record showing only a bot's read, with no trace of his call, never becomes his graded call.

COIN: his typed 3M lines name no coin; all are graded against Litecoin — his coin, the coin the 3M doctrine was taught on, and the standing house rule where no coin is named. Every such description says so plainly.

GRADING (his mechanical doctrine, exactly as the 3-minute gate runs it): over the two 3M Heikin-Ashi candles after the call candle — SLOWING is a HIT only when both following candles are littler than the call candle AND no fresh ground is made in the called direction (fresh ground forces PUSHING regardless of candle size); otherwise a MISS. PUSHING is a HIT when fresh ground is made, a MISS when the slowing gate fires instead, UNGRADED when the tape settles neither. Gappy or missing tape is UNGRADED with the reason stated — a grade is never guessed.

The grading recipe is saved at grade_3m_backfill.py beside this ledger; the fetched Bitunix tape is cached at tape_ltc_3m_cache.json so every grade can be re-derived.

The misses that prove the rules

Strict-rule misses keep their footnotes. They are never re-graded.

Row W2-01 — LTC, Oct 24, 5:04 AM MISS

Called a −$0.92 CYCLE down at $56.22. Price then fell $1.16 — 193% of the cycle number. Direction right, size right — but before the run, price bounced +$0.32, two cents past the $0.30 half-floor line. Adverse-first is a miss under the locked rules. It sits on the sheet as a miss, footnote and all.

Row B07 — BTC, Week 1 MISS

Price first pulled back $349.40, crossing the $250 half-floor — then traveled $1,293.90 favorable and the spread peaked at +1,999 that candle. The forward-path rule grades the pullback-first sequence a miss. Disclosed in full on the row, never quietly flipped to a hit.

Row B23 — ETH, Week 1 MISS

ETH first bounced $18.37 — over the $15 half-floor — then fell $41.05. The drop came; it came after the adverse line was crossed. Miss, by the mechanical rule. A record that only counts the convenient rows isn't a record. This one counts the rule.

The comeback misses

Went the other way first — past the grading floor — then came back and ran for him. All 27 still grade MISS.
27

of the 169 misses in the week ledgers first went against the call — then came back and ran in his favor anyway.

The biggest: W3-03 (BTC, Nov 4) — price traveled $331.9 against the call, past the $250 half-floor, then ran $2,878.5 for him — 507% of the call number. The closest: W2-28 broke adverse-first by six cents, then ran 194% of the number. Both read MISS on this sheet, and both always will.

Split of the 27: Week 1 · 2 — Week 2 · 10 — Week 3 · 15. By coin: BTC 11 · ETH 14 · LTC 2.

Read this plainly: the miss stands. Under the strict rule locked Oct 24, a call that crosses the grading floor the wrong way first is a MISS — even when price later comes all the way back and runs past the number. No grade on this page changes because of this section, and no total moves: these 27 sit inside the 169 misses of the three week ledgers — the calls book as a whole, the 618 three-minute calls counted in, now reads 1,180 calls — 391 HIT · 11 PARTIAL · 9 SHORT · 629 MISS · 140 UNGRADED. This section exists so the full picture is on the record: how far each one went against him first, and how far it then ran for him.

How the 27 were counted — mechanically, from the three ledgers, never by hand: a row graded MISS whose ledger note records the adverse-first strict-rule pattern (price crossed the half-floor against the call before the run) and whose forward run then reached at least 80% of the call number — the hit line under the 20% range rule (the ledgers' pct_of_call field; Week 1 rows carry no pct field, so theirs is measured against the band floor). 76 other misses carry an adverse-first note too, but the run back stopped short of the line — they are plain misses, and they are not in this table.

Early Week 1 windows were graded at 1h/15m granularity where 3m history doesn't reach; that is noted on the affected rows in the ledger. Log-vs-tape disagreements found during grading are flagged on their rows, not smoothed over. This page is a snapshot built Nov 15, 2026 — the live record keeps grading at every 6H candle close.

Not financial advice. This page documents a public track record; past graded calls do not guarantee future ones — the misses above are the reminder.
